Ballys Intralot (BYLOT-GR) · Investment memo

Ballys Intralot: a lean UK online engine inside a geared, owner-run group. At EUR 1.117 the shares already price in a half-delivered Evoke acquisition, so the stock is a watch-list case with a dated entry point in H1 2027

Analyst memo, 3 November 2026. Price EUR 1.117 (29 October 2026); about 1,868m diluted shares; market value EUR 2.09bn; company-adjusted net debt EUR 1.62bn at June 2026 (4.05x EBITDA); enterprise value about EUR 3.7bn. Next dated event: Q3 results, 27 November 2026.

How to read the numbers. Forecasts are the Financial Analyst's model after update 2 for the current group without Evoke ("standalone"); Evoke is added as a probability-weighted overlay. EBITDA is the company's adjusted EBITDA. EPS is adjusted (before acquired-intangible amortisation and exceptional items) unless marked "reported". EV/EBITDA is the valuation anchor. End note 1 gives the full conventions.

#0Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

What the company is. Ballys Intralot is two businesses moving in opposite directions, and its balance sheet and ownership structure will decide the equity outcome.

The engine is Bally's International Interactive (BII), a UK-centred online casino and bingo operator. BII is the leanest operator in its market: it spends about 11% of revenue on marketing against Evoke's 23%, earns a 35% EBITDA margin after paying a 40% duty, and grew its UK revenue 11-13% through the first duty step.

The legacy business is Intralot's lottery technology. It is number three in an oligopoly and is losing the tender cycle to better-capitalised rivals.

Around both businesses sit leverage, a controlling parent and a pending deal. Bally's Corporation owns 58% and carries a going-concern warning. The pending acquisition of Evoke would roughly double consolidated EBITDA.

The six conclusions that matter for the decision.

  1. 1
    BII is better than the group, and UK demand has not flinched at the duty. BII's UK online growth in constant currency accelerated from +6.3% in Q4 2025 to +10.5% in Q1 2026, +11.6% in Q2 and +13.0% in July, with record net gaming revenue and stable active customers, while the duty step cut the quarterly margin from 37.4% to 30.6%. Part of that growth is price taken from players through lower bonuses and a lower return-to-player. The real volume test is therefore still ahead: the first two quarters of 2027, against record comparatives and after the generosity cuts of H2 2026.
  2. 2
    The company's own guidance does not add up, and a rebase is likely on a known date. FY2026 EBITDA guidance of about EUR 422m exceeds the chief executive's own divisional outlook (BII EUR 280-295m plus legacy EUR 100-105m, or EUR 380-400m) and our EUR 385m. The FY2027 target of EUR 454m is 12% above our EUR 400m. We put a 65% probability on a cut or reframe of guidance at the Q3 results on 27 November. Two facts soften the damage: UK growth since July (+13%) has tilted the FY2026 risk slightly upward, and our reported-basis EPS path already sits close to the only visible broker forecast, so EPS estimates have less to lose than EBITDA estimates.
  3. 3
    Without Evoke, Ballys Intralot resets its margin and then repairs slowly; it is not a growth case. The duty permanently takes about five points off the group EBITDA margin (from about 40% to 35-36%). About EUR 95-100m a year of self-help defends the margin rather than creating growth. Standalone EBITDA regains its FY2025 level (EUR 431m) only in FY2029. Free cash flow to equity is about zero in FY2026 and reaches EUR 160m by FY2030, and leverage falls from 4.0x to 2.6x by FY2030, while the company's 2.5x target has already moved twice. Adjusted EPS nonetheless compounds at about 10% a year from a small base, because interest costs fall and each 1% change in EBITDA moves adjusted net income by about 3.6%.
  4. 4
    The Evoke acquisition is the investment case: a geared option on GBP 180m of cost synergies. Evoke's GBP 2.2bn enterprise value rests on only GBP 243m of equity, at 5.2x leverage. FY2028 adjusted EPS with Evoke is about EUR 0.093 if 85% of the synergies are delivered (30% probability), EUR 0.066 if half are delivered (42%), EUR 0.040 if volume losses absorb them (13%) and EUR 0.055 if the deal fails (15%). The probability-weighted figure is about EUR 0.069, against EUR 0.055 standalone. Each GBP 10m of delivered synergy is worth about EUR 0.044 a share at a fair multiple. Evoke's debt is not sealed off from the group, despite its "credit silo" label: the group has committed to support a GBP 200m prepayment by December 2027, the debt pays an 11% cash coupon and carries cross-default language, and Fitch caps Evoke's rating two notches above the parent's B-.
  5. 5
    The price already assumes a half-delivered Evoke. At EUR 1.117 the standalone business trades at 9.7x FY2026 and 9.3x FY2027 EBITDA. That is above every listed peer (Entain 5.6-7.8x, Evoke 5-6.3x, Brightstar about 5x, Lottomatica 5.8-8x) and above the multiples both brokers use in their own sum-of-the-parts valuations. Including Evoke at half the synergies, the same price is 7.7x FY2028 EBITDA. The market is therefore paying either a fair multiple for a half-delivered Evoke or a rich multiple for the standalone business, and it is not paying for the downside tails. At our 8.0x fair multiple (#11) the shares are worth about EUR 0.90 standalone at end-2027 (an 18% loss), EUR 1.27 with Evoke at half the synergies (+14%) and EUR 1.55 at full delivery (+40%): about EUR 1.26 (+13%) probability-weighted. Over three years the same arithmetic gives +7% standalone and about +48% probability-weighted, and the Evoke cases are the most exposed to the multiple (one turn is worth EUR 0.38 a share with Evoke, against EUR 0.22 standalone).
  6. 6
    The risk/reward skew is not positive today, but it can turn positive in H1 2027 on conditions that can be tested. Three facts keep the skew negative now. First, each of the next three dated events (the parent's Q3 filing, the 27 November results, and the resolution of the Evoke share-or-cash election, financing and Fitch rating) is more likely to widen the downside tail than to surprise positively. Second, the shares have not paid for the sector's de-rating: they returned +4.6% over twelve months against -30% to -68% for peers, with an R-squared to the sector of only 1%. Third, the balance sheet can turn a modest operating miss into a discontinuity: reported leverage of 4.05x already exceeds the 4.0x covenant on the Greek retail bond, and the waiver of that test expired on 8 October. The skew turns positive once the three conditions below are visible. That setup, an EPS step-up driven by a Big Corporate Change and bought at a fair multiple, is four to six months away on the calendar.
Condition 1: a beatable baseStandalone guidance and estimates rebased to EUR 385-400m of FY2026 EBITDA or lower, so that they can be beaten.
Condition 2: UK volume holdsUK volume holds through H1 2027. Regulus's -12% UK market scenario marks the bear case; Entain's +14% marks the bull case.
Condition 3: a clean EvokeEvoke completes cleanly, and the phasing of its synergies is in print.
What would pull the entry forwardQ3 results on 27 November with UK growth above 12%, a BII margin near 37% and a credible reaffirmation of guidance.

Implication. Richard should treat Ballys Intralot as a dated watch-list case, not a current position. BII's quality and the gearing of EPS to Evoke's synergies are real, but the right entry point comes after the guidance rebase and the Evoke election. Until then, the downside to a fair trough value (6.5-7x FY2026 EBITDA, or EUR 0.49-0.60 a share, a 46-56% fall) is larger than any near-term upside.

#1Operating environment: tailwinds, headwinds and risks

Conclusion: UK online demand is a genuine tailwind that has so far beaten the enacted tax headwind on volume. But the price-led part of that growth annualises and the offshore test is still ahead, so the operating environment is net adverse into mid-2027 and balanced thereafter.

The structural tailwind is online migration plus tax-driven consolidation. Online is projected to rise from 34% to 42% of global gross gaming revenue by 2030. In the UK, where online penetration is already 58-67%, growth comes from share gains instead, and the 40% duty is removing the sub-scale tail of about 200 companies that together hold 31% of the market. The ITV Win online casino closed within four months, about a dozen operators are seeking a sale, and Eilers & Krejcik expect six groups to hold two-thirds of the market by 2028.

Scaled peers confirm that UK demand is intact. Entain's UK online revenue grew 14% in Q2 and Q3 2026 (gaming +17%, active customers +15%), and Regulus estimates that the UK online market grew 12% in Q2 "with no visible impact" from the duty.

The UK tax headwind is enacted, dated and front-loaded. Remote Gaming Duty rose from 21% to 40% on 1 April 2026, a gross cost of EUR 95m in FY2026 and about EUR 127m annualised. Remote betting duty rises from 15% to 25% in April 2027, which matters little for a casino-led business. Fiscal tightening is also under way in the Netherlands, Romania, Greece and Brazil.

Each price step in the regulated market raises the latent risk that players leak offshore. The UK black market is 8-10% of the industry and could grow 50-100% after the tax rise; UK players made about 2m visits to unlicensed sites in June 2026; and the Netherlands lost 23-25% of its regulated revenue after its duty rose to 34.2%.

In lottery supply the environment is adverse. Scientific Games, under Brookfield ownership, bids aggressively (as in Ohio); Allwyn and OPAP combined in March 2026; US states unbundle tenders and bring platforms in-house; and renewals reprice downwards (Montana from 8% to 5% of stakes).

The October 2026 Budget clears the UK tax outlook for twelve months. It raised Machine Games Duty to 25%, which is irrelevant to a digital group, added no further Remote Gaming Duty rise, and was called "better than feared" by brokers.

Inference and so-what. The forces are net negative for six to twelve months and roughly balanced over three years, because the headwinds arrive before the tailwinds. The headwinds are certain and dated: Q1 2027 annualises the casino duty (about EUR 32m), and the Ohio and Morocco contracts end in mid-2027. The tailwinds are structural but slower.

The largest tailwind, consolidation share, is not yet in BII's own numbers. BII has grown with the UK market, not ahead of it, and its share has been flat at 14-15% since 2020. The group is buying consolidation share through Evoke rather than earning it.

The change in trend is the lens that matters. BII accelerated into the duty, which is the strongest external fact in the case, but the acceleration is partly price-led and annualises from Q2 2027.

Counter-case. The consolidation tailwind could be larger and faster than I allow. Customer databases are changing hands at royalty-style prices, Entain has gained three points of share in two quarters, and BII's low marketing intensity lets it absorb the departing operators' customers at marginal cost. If BII's UK growth stays above 12% through H1 2027 while active customers rise, the model's EUR 15m consolidation delta is too small and the FY2027 BII revenue range (EUR 790-840m) is too low.

What would change my view. Rising UK active customers and first-time depositors, not just rising revenue, in the Q3 and Q4 2026 results; or, against the case, a Regulus-style 2027 market contraction appearing in the Q1 2027 trading update.

Market versus me. Equity analysts (Jefferies, Barclays) read BII's +11.6% and Entain's +14% as proof that the duty is absorbed; credit analysts (Deutsche Bank, Regulus) see 2027 as the year the full cost shows. I side with the credit view on margins and with the equity view on volume. That is why my FY2027 UK growth assumption (+6% in constant currency) sits below the equity analysts' 8-10%, and why I widened the FY2027 range rather than raising it.

Score: 30, set by the Rater. An enacted Remote Gaming Duty rise from 21% to 40% on the largest profit pool permanently takes about five points off group margin (EUR 127m annualised, Q1 2027 still to annualise), and the lottery tender cycle is turning against the company (Ohio and Morocco lost, Montana repriced from 8% to 5%), with offshore leakage the direct threat to UK demand; against that, UK online demand is growing 11-13% and tax-driven consolidation is a real but slower, not-yet-earned tailwind, and the October Budget clears further duty for twelve months. Net clearly adverse over two to three years, close to the External change forces group's 28, just below Zegona's weak-but-stable market and above Volati's late-cyclical volume declines.

#2Internally-driven corporate change forces

Conclusion: the corporate change forces are broad, fast and delivering what management controls operationally. But they are funded with debt, governed for the parent, and have not yet kept a single financial promise, so I grade them as real but unreliable.

The change is total and fast. Within about a year the company gained a new controlling owner (October 2025) and a new chief executive who also runs the parent (Robeson Reeves, formerly of Gamesys, from 7 November 2025). The founder and the legacy chief executive moved to non-executive roles, the chief technology officer left, the IFRS 8 segments were redefined, the technology stack was unified in late 2025, and over USD 15m of corporate overhead was removed. The company also launched two transformational deals in eight months: BII at EUR 2.7bn, and Evoke at a GBP 2.2bn enterprise value, launched before BII's EUR 41m of synergies had landed.

Delivery on operating levers has been quick and dated. Management secured EUR 11.3m of permanent cost mitigation in the first duty quarter, entered new markets in four weeks on the simplified technology stack, and recorded six lottery wins or extensions in 2026 (Ontario, Ireland, Chile, Hellenic Lotteries, Arkansas, Victoria, British Columbia).

Delivery on financial promises has not followed. Leverage rose from 3.46x to 4.05x in six months. The 2.5x leverage target moved from "within two years" to FY2028-FY2029, and our standalone path reaches only 2.6x, in FY2030. The duty-mitigation metric was redefined four times, and management conceded that the plan is a year late. Distributions restarted from zero, but were paid from reserves while the company reported losses: a EUR 30m dividend, of which EUR 17.86m went to the parent, and a EUR 20.8m buyback through a total return swap.

Governance is weak and favours the parent. Executive pay rose 52% to EUR 8.5m with no disclosed performance hurdles and no equity component. The chief executive owns no shares. The audit and remuneration committees have identical members. Payables to the parent rose from EUR 11.74m to EUR 30.31m in six months, and the company holds a EUR 16.83m interest-bearing receivable from a parent with a going-concern warning.

Inference and so-what. The internal force is large and real at the input layer, but unproven at the output layer: it has produced no upgrade, no margin gain and no deleveraging yet. Its character is a dealmaker-operator running the subsidiary for the parent's strategy and financing every move with debt or reserves. That shape suits an earnings step-up if the deals work, and it is the wrong shape for a balance sheet with no buffer.

The sequence also matters. The company took on Evoke before proving BII, so the market will be asked to price Evoke's integration before it has seen BII's synergies.

Counter-case. The chief executive's Gamesys record (revenue from GBP 340m to GBP 709m in two years, leverage from 3.8x to 1.1x, 94% cash conversion) is exactly the playbook Evoke needs: a data-led, low-marketing casino operator absorbing a competitor that spends more on marketing. The 65% duty mitigation delivered within one quarter (Q2) shows the same capability. If Evoke's marketing ratio falls from 23% toward 16% of revenue in the first year without volume loss, the internal force is strong enough to carry the case on its own.

What would change my view. A quarter of deleveraging delivered rather than restated; an equity award to the chief executive tied to per-share outcomes; or, against the case, any cash moving to the parent beyond the dividend (intercompany charges, a parent cash call).

Market versus me. The sell-side credits the operating record and discounts the capital-allocation record only lightly (price targets EUR 1.35-1.41). For the next twelve months I weight the two records the other way round, because the equity outcome is decided below EBITDA.

Score: 57, set by the Rater. The company's own actions are very large and partly proven: a new owner and a chief executive with a strong Gamesys record, a unified stack, EUR 95-100m of self-help by FY2028 already running (EUR 11.3m in the first duty quarter), six lottery wins, and the Evoke acquisition, a large strategic move that lifts probability-weighted FY2028 EPS about 25% above standalone (EUR 0.069 against 0.055); offsetting this, no financial promise has yet been kept (leverage 3.46x to 4.05x, the 2.5x target moved twice, mitigation redefined four times) and governance is run for the parent with no incentive alignment. I sit above the Internal change forces group's 38 because the brief counts a deal of Evoke's size as a large force and its expected earnings effect is positive, but only mildly so after funding and governance, below Odfjell's funded, deleveraging acquisition and above Reply's steady continuity.

#3Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile, management

Conclusion: a favourable, consolidating UK online market and a genuine cost and data advantage in BII are set against a lottery business that is losing its tender cycle and a group financial profile that is below average on returns, cash to equity, earnings quality and leverage, run by an ambitious but unaligned management.

Both markets are concentrated and hard to enter (table below). In UK online the duty acts as a tax on lack of scale, and with Evoke BII would hold about 25-27%, second only to Flutter. In lottery technology the company has a long contracted tail and a EUR 1.4bn backlog, but it lost Ohio, had its Maryland award rescinded and repriced Montana.

The two moats differ in kind. In lottery the moat is switching cost and contract duration, and it no longer beats rivals at renewal: its value lies in duration, not price. In UK online the moat is scale, data and cost (the Vitruvian personalisation engine, marketing 10 points of revenue below peers, a 43% pre-duty margin), and it widens with each tax and compliance step. Neither half has pricing power in the framework's sense: consumer price rises only pass the tax through, and business-to-business prices are conceded at tender.

The financial profile is strong at EBITDA and weak below it. At EBITDA the group earns a 35-40% margin and converts 85-88% to cash before interest, helped by an asset-light consumer business. Below EBITDA the picture reverses:

  • total D&A of about EUR 172m and interest of about EUR 140m (36% of EBITDA);
  • reported losses (FY2025 EUR -65m; H1 2026 EUR -14m) and an adjusted-to-reported gap of EUR 70-80m a year;
  • returns on capital employed in low single digits against EUR 2.2bn of goodwill from BII alone;
  • free cash flow to equity near zero through the FY2026-FY2027 renewal-capex cycle.

Against peers, the margin is near the top and the leverage is near the worst (small table below). Only Lottomatica earns a higher margin, at lower leverage and with ten years of quarterly growth. FactSet's 5.8x leverage for Ballys Intralot is an artefact of mixed perimeters, but the company-basis 4.05x is still the highest of the listed set after Evoke.

Management is forceful and ambitious, but thin. It targets two new consumer markets a year and says "consolidation is here". Yet one chief operating officer holds four functions, there is no chief technology officer, staff turnover is 19%, and two cultures are being merged under cost-cutting.

Inference and so-what. BII's business model, a scaled UK online casino with data-led marketing efficiency, is a genuine above-average asset and the reason the investment case exists. The group around BII is below average on every financial-quality test Richard applies (returns, cash conversion to equity, earnings quality, leverage), and the lottery half is a melting but long-dated cash source rather than a moat. Management has stretching goals and the right direction, but not yet a winning culture or aligned incentives.

Counter-case. On a sum-of-the-parts basis the market is giving the lottery business away. Valuing BII in line with peers leaves legacy Intralot at about 2x EBITDA (Jefferies), despite a 16-year contract tail, four 2026 wins with modular products and USD 200m of Ohio capex avoided. And BII's quality is exactly what a consolidation cycle rewards.

What would change my view. Illinois renewed on Montana-or-better terms by mid-2027, together with a BII margin back above 38% and rising active customers, would move the group's financial profile from below average to around average.

Market versus me. Brokers' sum-of-the-parts valuations (Jefferies: 9.7x BII and 6x lottery; Deutsche Bank: 8x and 9x) agree that BII is a high-quality asset and disagree on the lottery half. I side with Jefferies on the lottery multiple, and I sit below both brokers on BII until it passes the UK volume test.

Score: 30, set by the Rater. Qualitatively, a concentrated high-barrier UK online market where BII is the lean number two with a widening scale and data moat sits beside a lottery business losing its tender cycle, no pricing power in either half and an ambitious but thin, unaligned management; the financial profile is weak below EBITDA (ROIC -3.8%, percentile 5; net margin percentile 3; 4x leverage; EUR 2.2bn of goodwill earning low single digits, and new capital deployed in BII and Evoke not yet earning its cost), and the EBITDA margin's 76th percentile overstates it. Coherent with the groups (50, 44, 15, 30): below Zegona, whose negative returns are similarly acquisition-driven but under a top-decile aligned owner-operator, and just above Instalco's fragmented, barrier-less model.

#4Guidance conservatism, expectation management, track record

Conclusion: guidance sits above the company's own arithmetic, has never been raised, and is managed by reframing rather than by setting beatable targets, so this topic scores low until the rebase has happened.

Formal guidance sits above both the sell-side and the company's own divisional arithmetic (#0, conclusion 2, and the chart below).

The record since the combination is short and slightly negative. FY2025 pro-forma EBITDA was EUR 430.8m against EUR 435m guided, 1% short, although revenue beat by 2%. Q4 2025 pro-forma EBITDA was 4% below consensus. Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of EUR 422m in May 2026 after a Q1 of EUR 100.2m; Q2 then came in at EUR 84.6m.

Management holds the headline and moves the building blocks, as the right-hand box below shows.

Disclosure and coverage are both thin. There has been no capital markets day since the combination and there is no guidance below EBITDA (D&A, interest, tax, free cash flow or EPS). The parent publishes the company's segments about two weeks before the company reports. The only visible broker EPS forecasts (Barclays: EUR 0.020, 0.030 and 0.040) sit near our reported path, and the FactSet FY2026 EBITDA "consensus" of EUR 408m has no visible contributor.

Inference and so-what. Guidance is not conservative once the duty run-rate is allowed for, and the company has no record of raising it. The next two results are the likeliest dates for a rebase: we put a 65% probability on a cut or reframe on 27 November, and at the FY2026 results the EUR 454m FY2027 target is more likely to be folded into a combined post-Evoke figure than cut explicitly.

The implication is twofold. A dated negative event lies ahead. After it, standalone numbers become beatable only if Evoke synergies are kept out of them, so a separate standalone guide is the one disclosure to insist on.

Counter-case. Q3 EBITDA above EUR 100m, with UK growth above 12% and no volume lost to the generosity cut, would let management "reaffirm" guidance and land FY2026 near EUR 400m; the AlphaSense guidance review gives "medium confidence" that the company meets or narrowly misses. The arithmetic says this outcome needs full mitigation and double-digit volume growth in the same quarter, and Q2 showed neither.

What would change my view. A standalone FY2027 target set at or below EUR 400-430m at the FY2026 results, with Evoke guided separately. That would be the first conservative number the combined group has published.

Market versus me. Deutsche Bank's credit research (EUR 390m) implicitly agrees with me; Jefferies' consensus of EUR 421m and the company's "on track" language do not. The gap between the market's numbers and mine is unfavourable for the shares, and it closes on a known date.

Score: 20, set by the Rater. The short record since the combination is a 1% FY2025 EBITDA miss, a 4% Q4 2025 miss against consensus, no raise ever, the leverage target deferred twice and the plan conceded a year late, and current FY2026 guidance of EUR 422m sits above the chief executive's own divisional arithmetic (EUR 380-400m) with a 65% chance of a cut on 27 November, managed by reframing rather than sandbagging; the sell-side revision figure (-65%, percentile 1) is a definitional artefact and adds little. In line with the Guidance and Sell-side groups (22, 22): a reaffirm-after-miss pattern that will be missed again, better than TT Electronics' chronic multi-year over-promising but well below Indutrade's mixed delivery.

#5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out and feedback loops

Conclusion: the business converts revenue into EBITDA at only 40-45%, but EBITDA into EPS at 3.6 times. Profit growth is therefore outsized at the per-share line, through financial gearing and the Evoke cost pool rather than through pricing power or operating leverage, and the same gearing makes the downside outsized.

The duty has weakened operating leverage in BII. Before April 2026 each extra unit of UK casino gross gaming revenue kept about 79% after duty; it now keeps about 60%. After content, payment and marketing costs, BII keeps about 40-45% of each extra unit of revenue as EBITDA, and about 55-60% of its post-duty cost base is variable.

The legacy lottery business runs operating leverage in reverse. Its cost base is fixed (staff are 45% of costs and cannot be cut without risk to service), so when revenue fell 6.5% in constant currency in H1 2026, EBITDA fell 13.6%.

Financial leverage is the dominant amplifier. Adjusted pre-tax profit is only about 30% of EBITDA, so a 1% change in EBITDA moves adjusted net income by 3.6% and reported net income by far more. Each EUR 100m of debt repaid at 7% adds EUR 0.003 of EPS. One turn of EV/EBITDA is worth 20% of the market value standalone and 34% with Evoke.

Standalone cost-out is large but mostly spoken for. EUR 41m of BII-Intralot synergies, about EUR 33m a year of duty-cost mitigation and EUR 25m from lower player generosity add up to about EUR 95-100m by FY2028, and the EUR 127m annualised duty absorbs almost all of it. The large pool is Evoke's GBP 180m. Cutting Evoke's marketing from 23% of revenue toward 16-17% over two years is feasible on precedent; cutting it to BII's 11% is not.

Only one of five feedback loops works in the company's favour, and it is not yet in BII's numbers. The most damaging is the business-to-business renewal loop: leverage limits renewal capex, platforms are lost or repriced, EBITDA falls and leverage stays high, taking legacy EBITDA from EUR 110m to EUR 85m by FY2028. The parent loop drains cash at the margin, the offshore loop is latent, the consolidation loop works at industry level only, and the deleveraging loop runs in slow motion standalone and is reset by Evoke.

Inference and so-what. Does revenue growth lead to outsized profit growth? At EBITDA, no: 5% BII revenue growth adds about EUR 15-17m, or about 4%. At EPS, yes, in both directions: that 4% becomes about 12% of adjusted EPS, and a 10% loss of UK volume takes 27% off it (#0 table).

The business has pricing power only as tax pass-through, and only modest operating leverage. What it has in abundance is financial gearing and, through Evoke, a cost-out pool worth almost half of standalone EBITDA. That combination is the mechanism of an EPS step-up driven by a Big Corporate Change, and also the mechanism of its failure.

Counter-case. The reinforcing loops could turn positive quickly. A customer database bought on royalty terms adds revenue at near-zero marketing cost; the margin on the GBP 400m term loan steps down 25 basis points once senior secured leverage falls below 3.25x; and Lottomatica beat every synergy target it set and re-rated to the top of its range.

What would change my view. Evidence that BII's incremental margin on growth exceeds 45% (the Q3 and Q4 BII margins against the 36-37% we assume), or that discounts on content fees (5-10% on fees worth about 22% of digital revenue) are landing.

Market versus me. The equity narrative treats the 65% duty mitigation as repeatable self-help. Two-thirds of it was organic growth that would have happened anyway, and I count each lever once.

Score: 42, set by the Rater. Operating leverage is modest (incremental BII flow-through about 40-45% with 55-60% of the post-duty cost base variable, so 5% BII growth adds only about 4% to EBITDA), pricing power is only tax pass-through, and the legacy B2B fixed cost base runs in reverse on falling revenue (revenue -6.5%, EBITDA -13.6% in H1 2026) inside a negative renewal-capex loop; what the model has is heavy but uncomfortable financial gearing (EBITDA to EPS 3.6:1 at 4x leverage, so the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio of about 4x reflects falling interest, not structure) and a large Evoke cost-out pool that is conditional. Below the ordinary 50 because the gears that work are financial and two-way, above 25 because the cost-out scope and gearing are real; coherent with the Financial forecasts group's 25 and Economic strength's 15 being lower, since those also weigh returns and the margin reset.

#6Forecast financials: growth and margins against the past

Conclusion: on a standalone basis the forecasts describe a permanently lower margin, 1-4% revenue growth and about 10% adjusted EPS growth from a reset base. Evoke is the only route to double-digit EBITDA growth and a near-doubling of EPS, so the growth case is per-share and conditional, not operational.

Evidence: the standalone forecasts (model after update 2). Three features of the table matter. Revenue grows only 1-4% a year. The EBITDA margin edges up from 34.8% to 35.9%. Adjusted EPS compounds at about 10.6% a year, while reported EPS rises from almost nothing.

The segments diverge. BII revenue rises from EUR 776m to EUR 929m at a 36-38% margin. Legacy revenue falls from EUR 331m to EUR 285m by FY2028 as Ohio and Morocco leave and Illinois reprices, and then grows about 3% a year once Ontario starts. Capex falls from EUR 170m in FY2026 (including the EUR 85m Victoria licence) to EUR 95m.

With Evoke, the per-share numbers step up (chart below). The overlay assumes completion on 1 April 2027 as an all-share deal issuing 252m new shares. For FY2029, group adjusted EPS is EUR 0.082 at half the synergies and about EUR 0.115 at 85%. Consolidated FY2028 EBITDA is about EUR 804-873m, at 4.0-4.8x leverage.

Inference and so-what. Set against the past, the forecasts answer four questions.

  • Is there scope for double-digit growth? Only at the adjusted EPS line (about 10% a year standalone, and a near-doubling by FY2029 in the full Evoke case), and only from below EBITDA: about two-thirds of the standalone EPS rise to FY2030 comes from EBITDA net of D&A, and a third from falling interest.
  • Is there scope for higher margins than in the past? None standalone (35-36% against 40-42%, because the duty is permanent), and lower still with Evoke because of business mix (about 27% combined).
  • Is there scope for faster growth than in the past? At revenue, no (1-4% against 4-8%). At EPS, yes, because the base has been reset.
  • Which way do I lean? FY2026 slightly up (July +13%, Entain +14%) and FY2027 down (the volume test, Illinois, Turkey). The uncertainty range around EPS is two and a half times as wide as the range around EBITDA.

Counter-case. Our FY2027 EBITDA of EUR 400m could be EUR 20-30m too low if UK growth holds at 10% rather than 6% and the consolidation delta arrives; that would add EUR 0.008-0.012 to EPS (+16-24%). It could be EUR 30m too high if the Regulus 2027 scenario plays out.

What would change my view. The purchase-price-allocation note in the FY2026 annual report (acquired-intangible amortisation is our EUR 57m estimate, and each EUR 10m changes adjusted EPS by EUR 0.004), and UK active customers in the Q1 2027 trading update.

Market versus me. My EBITDA is 9-12% below guidance in both years. My reported EPS is near Barclays, and my adjusted EPS is well below the September 2026 adjusted EPS series (EUR 0.072-0.097), which needed guidance-level EBITDA. The sell-side's 2% compound EBITDA growth (Deutsche Bank) is close to my 3-4%; the company's 7.6% growth to EUR 454m is the outlier.

Score: 75, set by the Rater. About 10% a year sits at the very floor of the 10-15% B band; the reported-basis path (EUR 0.003 to 0.047) and the 33% consensus next-year figure are base and definition artefacts, and the Evoke upside is a conditional overlay, so I rest on the adjusted standalone line. Placed at the bottom of the band because the growth comes from a duty-reset base with a third from falling interest, revenue grows only 1-4% against 4-8% in the past, and the margin path (35-36%) stays well below the 40-42% of FY2023-FY2025, though the growth is organic rather than bought.

#7Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over 6-12 months

Conclusion: the next six months are skewed to cuts in guidance and estimates, and the following six to conditional, modest upgrades. The scope for upgrades is therefore negative first and positive second, with the turning point around the FY2026 results.

Visible estimates sit above ours on both EBITDA (chart in #4) and EPS: Barclays forecasts FY2026 EPS of EUR 0.020, against our reported EUR 0.003. The FY2027 figure of about EUR 448m applies Deutsche Bank's growth rate to EUR 431m.

Recent data have improved, but only slightly. Since the current forecasts were set, volume data have moved up (BII's July +13%, Entain's Q3 +14%, Betsson's early Q4 +11%). At 40-45% flow-through that is worth only EUR 3-5m of FY2026 EBITDA. The Budget also removed the risk of a further duty rise for twelve months.

Mechanical changes will distort the screens. Consolidating Evoke in H1 2027 will roughly double FactSet EBITDA and raise brokers' EPS by 20-80% through changes of definition; these will register as upgrades and will not be real ones. Coverage will also broaden on the combined group (UK brokers initiating, Jefferies returning), probably from H2 2027. That broadening is the one genuine source of positive breadth in estimate revisions.

Inference and so-what. Over the first six months, upgrades are unlikely and cuts are likely; the figure below sizes them. Over months six to twelve, the scope turns conditional and modestly positive. Rebased standalone numbers can be beaten: our FY2026 range is EUR 375-398m with the risk skewed up, and our FY2027 range is EUR 370-425m with the risk skewed down but with a capped upside of about EUR 25m from consolidation share and content discounts. New coverage will also arrive with a narrative of 25-27% UK share.

Counter-case. If 27 November brings Q3 EBITDA above EUR 97m, UK growth above 12% and a BII margin near 37%, the rebase becomes a non-event and FY2026 lands near EUR 395-400m. The narrative would then flip to "absorbed the duty" six months early, and the share price would react to upgrades from a base that nobody had cut.

What would change my view. The Q3 results against those three markers, and the perimeter of FY2027 guidance (standalone shown separately, or hidden inside a combined figure).

Market versus me. The sell-side's momentum case (Jefferies) expects upgrades from consolidation now. I expect them only after a rebase, and only if UK volume passes the H1 2027 test. I expect the perimeter-driven screen "upgrades" of 2027 to fool the market for a few months, which would support the shares tactically but not fundamentally.

Score: 16, set by the Rater. Over the first six months the line that counts most is likely cut (65% probability of a cut or reframe of the EUR 422m FY2026 guide on 27 November, FY2027's EUR 454m likely folded or lowered), and EBITDA consensus is expected to fall 3-8% for FY2026 and 5-12% for FY2027, which against revenue growth of about 2% is a scaled downgrade of several times; the EPS line has less to lose because the only visible broker already sits near the reported path, the Evoke perimeter will produce screen 'upgrades' that are not real, and months six to twelve offer only conditional, capped upgrades from rebased numbers and new coverage. Coherent with the fourth-set group's 15: below Entra's continued estimate pressure because a guidance cut is likely, above Bally's because a beatable base and a positive second half are visible.

#8Current momentum: guidance, sell-side, narrative, technicals, and peers

Conclusion: guidance, estimate and narrative momentum are all negative, and the share price has held up only because flows rather than fundamentals drive it. That is a fragile kind of strength ahead of a dated rebase.

Evidence, leg by leg.

  • Guidance: held, not raised; a rebase is ahead.
  • Sell-side: the dashboard holds no earnings-momentum rating. FactSet's EPS series shows falls of 65-72% over three and six months, which reflect a change of contributor and definition rather than a cut, but are what the screens show. The mean target price is up 4% over six months, buy ratings are flat at 50% of analysts, and the revision-momentum score is -2.
  • Narrative: a debate between two houses, Jefferies' consolidation-momentum case against Deutsche Bank credit's tax-and-leverage case. Nobody has written up the covenant and parent questions. The market casts the stock as "the Evoke acquirer" within a sector story of tax de-rating, with post-Budget "clearing event" relief for Rank and Entain.
  • Technicals (dashboard, 29 October): technical momentum rated C; the price is 4.4% above its 200-day average, which rose in seven of the last twelve months; relative-strength percentile 49; returns of +2.0% over three months, +1.3% over six, +9.2% over nine and +4.6% over twelve; a 52-week range of EUR 0.81-1.20; average daily traded value of about USD 3m; and an R-squared to the peer basket of 1%, down from 20-25% in mid-2025 and collapsing at each deal.
  • Peers: Entain and Flutter rate F on both technical and earnings momentum, Allwyn F on both, and Evoke (as a bid target) and Lottomatica B on technical and D on earnings momentum. Valuation ratings are A for Entain, Flutter, Allwyn and FDJ, against C for Ballys Intralot at a 29.8x screen P/E.

The gap between the stock's +4.6% and its peers' -30% to -68% is an unpaid bill, not relative strength.

Inference and so-what. Fundamental momentum is negative on every leg, while price momentum is neutral and detached from the sector. The detachment is the important reading. In a 41% free float, the price is set by the parent's purchases (USD 42.7m in H1 2026, now limited by the parent's own covenants to the EUR 50m swap at the subsidiary), by Evoke arbitrage flows (investors shorting the acquirer against a target trading 13% below the offer value) and by index effects, not by sector factors. So no sector floor will support the price when the company's own news turns, and no sector lift will arrive when peers re-rate.

Counter-case. The post-Budget clearing event is real for the sector, and Ballys Intralot's casino-led book, with no retail shops, is the cleanest beneficiary of "no further Remote Gaming Duty rise". If the stock's correlation to the sector re-establishes, as it did in mid-2026, the stock could share the peers' relief rally.

What would change my view. A rising 200-day average with rising volume through the 27 November results; the revision score turning positive on a constant perimeter; a third equity house initiating coverage with published arithmetic.

Market versus me. The dashboard's C ratings for technicals and valuation understate how negative fundamental momentum is, because the sell-side legs are thin. I read momentum as D overall.

Score: 34, set by the Rater. Both measures are negative, which gives D; relative strength at 49 is only just below neutral and the price is 4.4% above a rising 200-day average, but the other parts confirm rather than contradict the letter: guidance held above its own arithmetic with a rebase ahead, EPS revisions of -65% to -72% on the screens (largely a definitional change, but no positive revision on a constant basis), Buy share flat at 50%, and a narrative split between equity and credit. Placed in the lower-middle of the band because fundamental momentum is negative on every leg and the price strength is flow-driven and detached from peers; peers at F are not used to pull it down.

#9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

Conclusion: the key drivers are few, dated and trackable, which is the case's one structural advantage. But the assumptions beneath them (volume elasticity, the covenants, the parent, the Evoke silo) are fragile, and the share-price risks are sudden, partly non-fundamental and material: the case is simple to follow and hard to hold.

The forecast is simple. Four items account for about 80% of the gross movement in EBITDA to FY2030: the Q1 2027 duty annualisation, UK volume growth at 40-45% flow-through, dated self-help, and the legacy exits and repricing. Three of the four are already enacted, contracted or delivered. Interest is mostly fixed and long-dated (maturities 2029-2031, about 54% fixed), so a 10% move in floating rates costs only about EUR 1m.

The operating drivers are trackable; the financial ones are not. The company reports UK growth monthly in trading updates, mitigation by lever in euros, divisional EBITDA each half and leverage each quarter, and the parent publishes the segments two weeks earlier. What cannot be tracked is the acquired-intangible amortisation, the covenant definitions, a free cash flow that includes licences and interest, the terms of the Illinois renewal, and related-party cash flows.

Fragility sits in five places, summarised in the table below with their mitigants. Three details matter beyond the table:

  • The volume elasticity after the H2 2026 generosity cuts is untested: high-value (VIP) players notice a 0.5% change in return-to-player, and Rank's growth slowed from +12% to +6% when it cut marketing.
  • The covenant definitions are unresolved, and clarifying them is the first research request.
  • The parent does not project covenant compliance after its waiver ends in Q1 2027, and its ring-fencing holds at the debt level but not at the cash level.

The share-price risks are sudden and material. About 252m Athens-listed shares will flow back to UK holders of Evoke, arbitrage shorts will persist until completion, the free float is thin, and the screen P/E of 30x compares with 6-15x for peers. The credit market is also punishing levered complexity: European high-yield spreads widened 65 basis points in October, the group's 2031 notes yield 7.5% and Evoke's 12.5%.

Sector precedents point the same way. After the 2014 Point of Consumption tax and the 2019 duty rise, UK volume held for two to four quarters and dispersion between operators appeared in the second year; the Netherlands case is set out in #1. Over 60% of highly levered lottery-technology mergers missed their deleveraging targets. Evoke, Entain and Intralot's own 2019-2021 history fit the archetype of a levered consolidator meeting a tax reset; Lottomatica is the counter-archetype, with domestic, repeated and lightly levered deals.

Inference and so-what. The forecast is predictable where it is boring and unpredictable where it matters. The 80% range for FY2026-FY2027 EBITDA is about plus or minus 4-7%. For EPS it is about plus or minus 20-25% standalone and nearly four times wider with Evoke (FY2028 EUR 0.024-0.089 on the old D&A basis), and the lower tail is fat for reasons that are not operational.

That distribution has the wrong shape for a levered equity: a reasonable probability of landing near EUR 400m of EBITDA, a not-small probability of a 40-55% drawdown from a tail event, and a low probability of an upside surprise of similar size until synergies are visible. The risks are prevalent (several are live now), partly non-fundamental (flows) and mostly dated, so careful timing can avoid most of them.

Counter-case. Every named tail has a mitigant. The Greek bond is only EUR 130m and its holders have waived once already. The parent's debt is secured on its stake, not on the company's assets, and the company guarantees none of it. Evoke's second-lien debt carries no parent guarantee. Liquidity is EUR 287m, including EUR 95m undrawn, and maturities are long. The base rate for levered gaming operators is renegotiation, not default.

What would change my view. The covenant note in the FY2026 annual report (which test, which EBITDA, Evoke in or out); the parent's Q3 10-Q filing and its waiver conditions; the Evoke cash election (the maximum cash option adds EUR 135m of debt and halves the flowback of shares).

Market versus me. The equity narrative treats the Evoke silo as sealed and the parent as irrelevant; the credit narrative treats both as first-order risks. I side with credit on the tails and with equity on the central path.

Score: 15, set by the Rater. The operating drivers are few, dated and trackable (EBITDA within about 4-7% for FY2026-FY2027), but the memo's next-year EPS range is about 20-25% either way standalone and nearly four times wider with Evoke, and the equity is exposed to sudden, partly non-fundamental tails: a 4.0x covenant on the Greek bond against 4.05x reported with the waiver expired, a controlling parent with a going-concern warning and porous ring-fencing, the Evoke silo's GBP 200m support and 11% coupon, the total return swap settlement, 252m shares of flowback and a 40-55% plausible drawdown. Coherent with the first-layer Risks group's 14 rather than the third-layer 28, because the balance sheet turns a modest miss into a discontinuity; between Instalco's levered, opaque roll-up and Teqnion's unreliable forecasts.

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: the stock is bottoming, with the rebase still ahead, and is not yet turning up. It has a visible route to thesis-broadening in H1 2027 and a visible route to collapse through the balance sheet.

Operationally, the company is at the end of a bottoming phase. EBITDA troughs in FY2026, BII is accelerating, the duty is now fixed for a year, and self-help is in the run-rate.

The expectations cycle lags behind the operations. Guidance has not been rebased, estimates have not been cut on a constant basis, the narrative has not absorbed the arithmetic, and the share price has not absorbed the sector's de-rating.

The next steps are therefore predictable. First comes a rebase (negative and dated). Then comes a change of perimeter as Evoke is consolidated, which will confuse the screens with upgrades that are not real. Then, if UK volume holds through H1 2027 and the first synergy phasing is in print, comes a thesis-broadening phase in which the stock becomes a combined-group scale story with new coverage.

The collapsing branch runs through the balance-sheet and owner tail (#9). A covenant event, a parent cash call or an equity raise would move the stock straight from bottoming to collapsing, without ever turning up.

Counter-case. If the 27 November results deliver the three markers set out in #7 (Q3 EBITDA above EUR 97m, UK growth above 12%, a BII margin near 37%), the stock is already turning up, and the bottoming phase ended with the Q2 margin.

What would change my view. The guidance language on 27 November (a framing of "BII EUR 280-295m plus legacy" is a cut, whatever it is called) and UK active customers in Q1 2027.

Market versus me. The brokers' targets of EUR 1.35-1.41 imply that they see the stock as turning up; the dashboard's Stage 2 bucket ("B_early") is consistent with my reading. I place the stock one step earlier in its lifecycle than the brokers do.

Score: 38, set by the Rater. Operationally the business is bottoming (EBITDA troughs in FY2026, the engine is accelerating, the duty is fixed for a year), but the expectations cycle is still ahead of it: guidance has not been rebased, estimates have not been cut on a constant basis, and the share price has not paid the sector's de-rating, so the next six months bring a negative, dated rebase and a confusing perimeter change before any broadening in H1 2027, with a visible route to collapse through the balance sheet and the parent. I agree with the memo's Bottoming but place it nearer Stalling than a clean bottom, below CVS's credible bottoming and Hellenic Telecom's late reinforcing and just above Storskogen's stalling.

#11The fair multiple

Conclusion: the fair multiple is 8.0x forward EV/EBITDA (about 15x two-year-forward adjusted EPS), in the lower half of the peer range because the stock is bottoming and levered. That is a 25-30% de-rating from today's standalone multiple, and roughly where the market already sits if it is looking through to a half-delivered Evoke.

The stock's own P/E history cannot set a guideline. The Phases data give no starting phase and no guideline fair multiple, because the stock's two-year-forward P/E history is unusable. It exists only for nine months of 2024 (28-44x) and three months of 2026 (9-10x), on a share count that rose twelve-fold and on earnings that were negative in most years. The current screen P/E of 30.3x rests on one broker's near-reported EPS. I therefore set the multiple myself, on EV/EBITDA, the basis on which the company and its peers are actually valued.

Evidence: today's multiple. Standalone, the shares trade at 9.7x FY2026 and 9.3x FY2027 EBITDA, at about 21x two-year-forward adjusted EPS on the model (the model's own 20.1x uses a price of EUR 1.09), and at 30x on the screen.

Evidence: peers and brokers. Peers trade at lower EV/EBITDA multiples (chart below). Evoke was bought at 6.3x pre-duty EBITDA, about 7.4x post-duty and pre-synergy on our numbers. Jefferies puts the UK online peer median at 7.6x "depressed" and 9.7x "tax-cleared". The brokers' sum-of-the-parts inputs blend to about 8.8x (Jefferies: 9.7x BII and 6.0x lottery) and about 8.3x (Deutsche Bank: 8.0x BII and 9.0x lottery, with a 30% leverage discount).

Evidence: precedents. Levered consolidators trade at the bottom of their ranges while leverage exceeds target (Evoke at 4.8-5.3x for three years). They re-rate over 18-36 months on deleveraging milestones, synergy upgrades and regulatory clearing events: Playtech-Snaitech cut leverage from 2.1x to 1.0x in 18 months and then exited at 9x; Entain sold its Central and Eastern European business at 10x against a trading multiple of 5.8x; Rank re-rated after the Budget. For a stock in a bottoming phase with uncertain forecasts, the base rate is the lower half of the range.

My view: 8.0x forward EV/EBITDA, built from two parts.

  • UK online (two-thirds) at about 7.5x: above Entain and Evoke, because BII's 35% post-duty margin and 11% marketing ratio are top-quartile; below Jefferies' tax-cleared 9.7x, because the volume test is unpassed and the business depends on one country.
  • Lottery (one-third) at about 7.0x: between Brightstar's trading multiple and Jefferies' 6x on one side and Deutsche Bank's 9x on the other. The contracts' duration deserves more than Brightstar's multiple; the tender losses deserve less than Deutsche Bank's.

8.0x is the top of the 6.5-8x range used in the third set of analysis and the bottom of the brokers' inputs. It is where a bottoming-phase stock with 4x leverage belongs, and it should rise toward 9x only once leverage is visibly below 3.5x and synergies are in print.

Translated into P/E terms, 8.0x FY2028 EBITDA at end-2027 equals about 15x two-year-forward adjusted EPS standalone (EUR 0.90 on EUR 0.059), about 22-24x on the screen's near-reported basis, and about 17x on Evoke-inclusive EPS. Against today's 21x adjusted and 30x screen multiples, the fair multiple is about 25-30% below the current standalone multiple.

Counter-case. With Evoke the group becomes the number-two UK online operator at 25-27% share, and consolidation precedents say the survivors re-rate to the top of their range: Italy's top two operators went from under 20% to over 55% share, and Lottomatica trades at the 75th-90th percentile of its own history. If the synergies land and combined leverage is heading below 4x by end-2028, 9x is defensible, and each turn is worth EUR 0.38 a share.

What would change my view. Leverage below 3.5x on the company basis, or two consecutive quarters of synergy phasing at or ahead of the guide of 75% in year one; either would move me to 8.5-9x.

Market versus me. The market pays 9.3-9.7x for the standalone business, or 7.7x for a half-delivered Evoke; the brokers' blended inputs are 8.3-8.8x. I am below the market on the standalone business and in line with it on the Evoke look-through.

Score: 30, set by the Rater. Figures.md holds no peer reading, so measure 2 comes from the memo's peer comparison, which puts the standalone business at a premium of 20% or more to every peer and 15-20% above the memo's 8.0x fair multiple and both brokers' blended inputs: dear on one, neutral on the other gives D. Placed in the lower part of the band because the neutral reading flatters (the ten-year P/E history covers twelve months on a share count that rose twelve-fold and on near-reported EPS), lifted off the floor only because a look-through to a half-delivered Evoke puts the price at about 7.7x, close to fair.

#12Total shareholder return via the DuPont split

Conclusion: on the standalone business the return to end-2027 is about -18%, because a 25% de-rating overwhelms 11% earnings growth. The positive returns (+13% probability-weighted at 18 months, about +48% at three years) come entirely from Evoke's synergy-geared earnings. The return is therefore a bet on delivery of a cost programme with no clean precedent, taken at a price that already assumes half of it.

The model's own return line cannot be used. The model's one-page summary computes +36.7% to end-2027 and +59.7% to mid-2029 at a "guideline fair multiple" of 0.00x, and its DuPont split (-154% from the multiple, -344% from earnings) is an artefact of that empty cell. I therefore calculate the return at the 8.0x fair multiple of #11, on the model's standalone forecasts and the Evoke overlay (end note 3).

The arithmetic (derived; claims on the enterprise value include net debt, leases and minorities):

  • End-2027, standalone: FY2028 EBITDA of EUR 408m at 8.0x gives EUR 3,264m; less claims of about EUR 1,600m (net debt of EUR 1,508m plus leases and minorities), equity is EUR 1,664m, or EUR 0.90 a share.
  • Mid-2029, standalone: next-twelve-month EBITDA of about EUR 433m at 8.0x, less claims of about EUR 1,310m, gives EUR 1.17 a share.
  • End-2027, with Evoke (completion April 2027, all-share, 2,097m shares, about EUR 2.15bn of Evoke net debt consolidated): at half the synergies, EBITDA of EUR 804m and claims of about EUR 3.76bn give EUR 1.27; at 85%, EBITDA of EUR 873m gives EUR 1.55; with synergies absorbed (Evoke EBITDA about EUR 310m), EUR 0.94.
  • Mid-2029, with Evoke: EUR 1.65 at half the synergies, about EUR 2.00 at full delivery and EUR 1.21 if absorbed.

Sensitivity to the multiple. One turn of EV/EBITDA is worth 20 points of return standalone and 34 points with Evoke. At 7.0x, the Evoke-half case is worth EUR 0.90 at end-2027 and EUR 1.25 at mid-2029; that is where the three-year return goes if the market keeps the group in Evoke's old valuation band because leverage stays above 4x.

Three things drive the return, in order of importance.

  1. The multiple. Standalone, the multiple must fall by about a quarter from today's level to reach fair value, and no plausible standalone earnings growth offsets that fall within 18 months. That arithmetic is why the current price can only be explained by the market paying for Evoke.
  2. Synergy delivery. The earnings part of the DuPont split swings from +11% to +40% to +70% across the Evoke cases, because GBP 180m of cost-out is added to a group with EUR 400m of EBITDA while the share count rises only 13%. Each half-tranche of the synergies is worth 24% of today's price.
  3. Time. The standalone case turns slightly positive at three years because deleveraging and interest savings accumulate (free cash flow to equity reaches about EUR 160m by FY2030 against a EUR 2.1bn market value; chart in #6). The standalone business is therefore not a short; it is a wait.

Dividends are immaterial (about 1% a year) and are paid from reserves in FY2026.

Counter-case. If the market holds a 9x multiple through the Evoke consolidation on a scale narrative with new coverage, the end-2027 Evoke-half value is EUR 1.65 (+48%) and the full-delivery value EUR 1.98 (+77%). The multiple would then lift the return instead of dragging on it, and the three-year annualised return would exceed 25%.

What would change my view. A first synergy phasing at or above 40% of the GBP 180m within two quarters of completion. That would shift the probabilities of the 85%, half and absorbed cases from 30/42/13 toward 45/40/5, and lift the probability-weighted end-2027 value to about EUR 1.37.

Market versus me. The brokers' targets of EUR 1.35-1.41 sit within my Evoke-half-to-full range on a 12-month view, which tells me they value the deal at a fair multiple as if it were delivered. My probability-weighted EUR 1.26 at end-2027 is 10% below them, because I weight the half and absorbed cases more heavily and expect the multiple to recover later.

Score: 52, set by the Rater. About +13% sits in the C band (10-20%), about 57 on the scale; the three-year check of about +48% is supportive but comes entirely from Evoke's synergy-geared earnings leg and a recovery of the multiple. Moved down to 52 for the fat lower tail: the standalone and no-completion cases (-18%, 15% weight) and the absorbed case (-15%) carry 28% of the weight, and the balance-sheet and owner tail (an equity issuance at EUR 0.80, a fair-trough value of EUR 0.49-0.60) lies outside the weighted figure.

#13Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Ballys Intralot owns one asset Richard would want to own: a UK online casino operator with the industry's leanest cost base and demand that has grown through a 40% duty.

Around that asset sits everything he would not want to own: a lottery supplier losing its tender cycle; 4x leverage, with covenant tests resuming at zero visible headroom on one instrument; a controlling parent with a going-concern warning and a shared chief executive; guidance that the company's own arithmetic contradicts; and an acquisition whose equity return is a geared option on a synergy target with no precedent, financed in the worst high-yield window since 2022.

The case for the shares is real and specific. If Evoke completes and delivers half its synergies, adjusted EPS rises about 40% by FY2028 and the shares are worth about EUR 1.27 at a fair multiple. At full delivery they are worth EUR 1.55, and the probability-weighted three-year return is close to 50%.

The case against holding the shares now is equally specific. At the same multiple the standalone business is worth EUR 0.90; the next three dated events are skewed to the downside; the sector's de-rating is an unpaid bill; and the balance sheet and the owner can turn a modest miss into a discontinuity.

The resolution is timing. The entry setup, an EPS step-up driven by a Big Corporate Change, at a fair multiple, with beatable standalone numbers, should become visible between the 27 November results and the FY2026 results in March-April 2027, and each of its three conditions can be tested (#0). Until then Ballys Intralot is a watch-list case with a dated trigger, not a position. A Q3 result on 27 November with UK growth above 12%, a BII margin near 37% and a credible reaffirmation is the one development that would pull the trigger forward.

52

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 52, set by the Rater. The input forces are large and pull against each other: an enacted duty and lottery repricing take margin permanently (topic 1, 30) while self-help and the Evoke deal are a large internal positive whose reach to profits is conditional on synergy delivery and funding (topic 2, 57); the financial output is about 10% a year of adjusted EPS from a reset base, roughly the Universe's typical rate, with EBITDA regaining its FY2025 level only in FY2029 (topic 6, B at 75). So the net change is near neutral, tilted just above 50 by the probability-weighted Evoke uplift, because the profit step-up is not yet visible and rests on an unproven cost programme.

26

Foundations' Robustness: 26, set by the Rater. A top-quartile, lean UK online engine in a concentrated market cannot make the group robust when the lottery half is losing its renewals, returns on capital are negative, the group carries 4x leverage and a distressed controlling parent shares its chief executive (topic 3, 30); and the delivery record of guidance held above its own arithmetic, never raised and with a leverage target deferred twice (topic 4, 20) adds no reason for trust. That is a narrow moat inside a weak, highly geared whole with a record of missed targets, about the 25 level.

50

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 50, set by the Rater. In substance the case is a genuine Big Corporate Change-driven EPS step-up: a new owner and an operator with the right playbook, a deal that roughly doubles EBITDA, and EPS geared about 0.044 a share per GBP 10m of synergy, so the setup's mechanism is present. But today's problems blur the fit: the deal is not completed, the synergies are unevidenced, guidance sits above the company's own arithmetic, and the covenant headroom and the parent's going-concern warning could force issuance or disrupt the step-up; timing and the standalone multiple are left to topics 7 and 12 and do not count here, which is why this sits at the fits-in-kind-but-misses-an-element level rather than the memo's lower D.

13

Case Riskiness: 13, set by the Rater. The few, dated and trackable operating drivers keep it off the very bottom, but the equity outcome is wide and fat-tailed (topic 9, 15): an EPS range of 20-25% either way standalone and four times that with Evoke, zero covenant headroom on one instrument, a parent with a going-concern warning, the Evoke silo and flow-driven price formation together mean a modest operating miss can become a balance-sheet event. Several of Richard's red flags compound here, so it sits near the 10 level, a little below topic 9.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
